storyboard.topic: Derivative as the limit of secants
storyboard.learning_objective: See why the slope of x² at x = 1 is 2, by watching secant lines turn into the tangent line.

beats.name: title
beats.description: Show the topic as the title

beats.name: curve
beats.description: Draw the curve and its label
beats.caption: Our curve: f(x) = x²
beats.narration: Here is the curve f(x) = x².

beats.name: point
beats.caption: Zoom in on P = (1, 1)
beats.narration: We want the steepness of the curve exactly at the point P = (1, 1).

beats.name: secant
beats.description: Add Q = (x0 + h, f(x0 + h)) and the secant PQ
beats.caption: Q sits h to the right of P
beats.narration: Pick a second point Q, a distance h to the right, and draw the line through P and Q.

beats.name: secant_pause
beats.description: Let the viewer read the slope
beats.caption: Secant slope = (f(x₀+h) − f(x₀)) / h
beats.narration: The slope of this secant line works out to Slope = 2 + h.

beats.name: shrink
beats.description: Shrink h toward 0; Q slides to P
beats.caption: Now let h shrink toward 0
beats.narration: Now slide Q toward P by shrinking h.

beats.name: shrink_pause
beats.caption: At h = 0.01: slope = 2.01
beats.narration: With h = 0.01 the secant slope is already 2.01.

beats.name: tangent
beats.description: Replace the secant with the tangent line
beats.caption: The secants become the tangent
beats.narration: In the limit, the secant lines become the tangent line.

beats.name: tangent_label
beats.caption: So f′(1) = 2
beats.narration: So the derivative at x = 1 is 2: the slope of the tangent line.
